instruction: User pool {{reference-architectures-Cognito-apilambda-us-east-1-UserPoolId}} has account recovery configured. A compliance auditor asks: if a user forgets their password, what is the actual recovery flow they will experience, and are there any recovery methods listed in the config that are not used today?
expected_answer: A user can recover via email; they will never be able to recover via phone, despite phone being listed as the priority-1 recovery mechanism. `aws cognito-idp describe-user-pool --user-pool-id {{reference-architectures-Cognito-apilambda-us-east-1-UserPoolId}}` shows `AccountRecoverySetting.RecoveryMechanisms` = [{Priority:1, Name:verified_phone_number}, {Priority:2, Name:verified_email}], so Cognito's own config claims phone is the preferred recovery path. But: (a) `SmsConfiguration` is null. The pool has no SNS role/ExternalId configured, so Cognito has no way to actually send a verification SMS to anyone. (b) `AutoVerifiedAttributes` = ["email"]. Phone numbers are NOT auto-verified on sign-up. Since the recovery mechanism specifically requires `verified_phone_number`, a user's phone number must first be verified via the SMS flow, which can't happen without SmsConfiguration. (c) `UsernameAttributes` = ["email"], and sign-up is blocked via AdminCreateUserOnly=true, so there's no self-service phone registration even if SmsConfiguration were added. Net: Cognito evaluates recovery mechanisms in priority order but skips any for which the user has no verified attribute. Since nobody in this pool can have a verified phone number, every password-recovery request falls through to priority-2 `verified_email`, and users receive the reset email. The phone mechanism is effectively dead config, a lint warning for the auditor. Separately, even the email recovery flow can't exercise today because the pool has zero app clients (`list-user-pool-clients` returns []), so there's no client_id to call ForgotPassword against. Once an app client is added, email recovery will work end-to-end; phone recovery will still not, and remains misleading.
